topic: Why SBOM (Software Bill of Materials) matters: lessons from the MOVEit Transfer RCE chain
post_text:
Here's what most organizations still get wrong about SBOM.

When Progress Software disclosed CVE-2023-34362 (MOVEit Transfer RCE), the initial response across most enterprises was predictable: patch the application. But that wasn't the hard part. The hard part was answering: "Do we even use MOVEit? Where? In what version?"

Without an accurate, maintained Software Bill of Materials, teams couldn't answer that question quickly. Some discovered MOVEit was embedded in third-party tools they'd forgotten they owned. Others found it running on systems they thought were decommissioned.

An SBOM is your supply chain inventory—not just a list of frameworks and libraries, but versions, dependencies, and where each component actually runs. Think of it like knowing every ingredient in your restaurant's supply chain: not just "we use tomatoes," but which farm, which harvest, which batch, and every dish that contains it.

The value isn't in the SBOM document itself. It's in what you can do with it:

• Rapid blast radius assessment when a CVE drops
• Identifying transitive dependencies (a library you don't directly use, but your vendor does)
• Detecting supply chain compromise earlier
• Automating vulnerability correlation across your estate

Post-MOVEit, enterprises that maintained SBOMs answered "Are we affected?" in hours. Others took weeks.

If you can't inventory your software, you can't secure it.

♻️ Repost if this helped someone.
